messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident opened: private-vpc cluster 'cust-nyc-1' experiencing GPU provisioning failures and request queue growth (>4.2k). Severity: P1. Pager assigned to @eng-oncall.
rohan: seeing steady inflight queue + throttling in the private router. New requests are 429s from the edge. Noticed a flurry of preemptible node terminations around 02:12 UTC.
maria: confirmed - autoscaler keeps trying to create nodes but many creations fail with 'preemptible-terminated' then 'quota/limit exceeded' errors. Provision logs: `ERROR: GCE API quota denied` and intermittent `AttachVolume timeout`.
samir: customer says their jobs started to accumulate ~10m ago. They reported slow responses and some request timeouts. CS on call is looped.
eng-oncall: taking this. quick triage: is this pure quota/preemption or something in our node bootstrap?
rohan: looks like mix: GCP preemptible churn + our scale-up hit nodeTemplate that still references deprecated image (image pull per-node times out) causing creation to hang then retry. Autoscaler backoff keeps hitting limits.
infra-lead: I see image registry rate-limiting in the project for this customer region. Also root cause: we launched a recent AMI update that increased init time (systemd units for monitoring). When preemptible nodes spin up they time out on attach and are deleted -> churn.
maria: queue metric: private-gpu-queue.length peaked at 4200, user-facing 429s at the ingress, latency p95 jumped to 12s then requests started to queue.
eng-oncall: immediate mitigation suggestions?
rohan: 1) Flip routing to hosted fallback pool for critical customers (canary only). 2) Lower model replica memory -> use 8-bit quantized variant for new requests. 3) Temporarily disable preemptible/spot nodes for this cluster to stabilize.
samir: CS: customer willing to accept degraded quality for short window if it reduces latency. They prefer hosted fallback over dropped requests.
eng-oncall: doing (1) now — adding route rule to divert 20% of traffic to us-hosted-1 for cust-nyc-1 flagged sessions. Applying policy.
incident-bot: Route change deployed by eng-oncall at 02:28 UTC. 20% diverted to hosted.
rohan: initiating change (2) — policy to fallback to quantized-8bit for non-premium requests in this cluster. Patching model config.
maria: starting manual intervention (3): scaling group change — set nodepool.preemptible=false and increase desired to +4. Handoff to infra to approve.
infra-lead: approved. Creating 4 standard (non-preemptible) GPU nodes manually to get immediate capacity. Command used: ```gcloud compute instances create ... --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-t4 --image=redwood-base-v3```
samir: progress: two nodes in RUNNING, one stuck in 'Attaching disk' for now. attach retries showing `rpc deadline exceeded`.
rohan: created a temporary warm pool in the cluster with taints to host customer pods only. Will remove when stable.
eng-oncall: after route + quantize + manual nodes, queue dropped from 4200 -> 800 over 12 minutes. 429 rate down from 7% -> 1.2%. Good sign.
customer-success: informed customer: "we diverted a small fraction to hosted and activated degraded model to lower latency; we're provisioning non-preemptible capacity now." They replied: "ok please keep us posted".
maria: still seeing some bootstrap failures for new nodes due to the image pull rate-limit. I've opened a ticket with registry team to lift limits for the next hour.
rohan: note: autoscaler config had aggressive backoff 10m which delayed effective scale for this burst. Recommend lowering initial backoff and enabling warm pools for private clusters. Logged a change request: CR-1043.
eng-oncall: recording impact: ~3k requests delayed, ~120 customers affected with transient errors, single-rep SLA breaches for 6 minutes.
incident-bot: Incident updated: mitigation in progress. Severity remains P1 until queue < 100 and error rate < 0.5%.
infra-lead: registry rate limit lifted by ops at 02:45 UTC. Attaches recovered, remaining nodes came up.
samir: all manual nodes healthy by 02:52 UTC. Autoscaler now sees additional capacity and scaled down the retry attempts.
maria: final metrics: queue back to 45, 429s dropped to 0.1%, p95 latency back to 230ms for hosted fallback and 420ms for private cluster (quantized).
eng-oncall: rolling post-incident tasks: 1) revert route rule (gradual) and plan controlled rollback of quantized fallback. 2) update nodeTemplate to new image that skips heavy init. 3) change autoscaler defaults for preemptible-heavy clusters. 4) add early-warning alert for image-pull-rate-limits.
rohan: creating postmortem skeleton and will include timeline + customer impact + CRs. Assigning owners: infra-lead for nodeTemplate fix, devex for warm-pools doc, eng-oncall for autoscaler tuning.
customer-success: customer happy with update and wants follow-up: please include timeline and compensatory credits if SLA breach confirmed.
eng-oncall: handing off to oncall-assignee for postmortem. tagging @sre-bot to create incident record.
sre-bot: Incident record created: INC-2026-3276543210. Postmortem in progress.
rohan: closing note: main root cause = combination of preemptible churn + slow image init + registry rate-limiting. Mitigation chain worked: route fallback + quantized model + manual non-preemptible warm nodes. Will keep monitoring for 2h. :white_check_mark:
eng-oncall: incident resolved from paging perspective. Monitoring window started. Will update once postmortem is published. :thumbsup:
